answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with a capped vouching graph: each established agent may vouch for only a few newcomers per season, backing each vouch with a bond that is slashed if the newcomer cheats. A single honest agent reaching the zenith of trust therefore cannot mint an army; it can sponsor only a small mesa of peers, not a flood. An attacker wanting hundreds of fake identities must bribe or compromise many unrelated sponsors and post a bond for each, so the cost grows linearly with every fake while the nectar of free influence shrinks, making a Sybil flood uneconomical.
